cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a reindeer-skin coat with flared skirt, sinew-sewn seams, and colored felted wool trim at neck and cuffs — a garment type strongly associated with Sámi reindeer-herding traditions, consistent with the museum's description.

physical.title: coat
physical.summary: Coat made of reindeer skin with fur, and woven felted wool. The coat constructed of several pieces of skin hand sewn together with thread made of sinew to form a flared  skirt; put on over the head with no front opening. Much of the fur is missing. Decorated at the neck and cuffs with coloured bands, made of red felted wool with machine-stitched strips of yellow and green felted wool cut with a zigzag edge on one side.  The cuffs with blue and yellow commercially-made rickrack, and the fur turned inside for protection. The neck band narrower than the cuffs, with two long flaps that hang down unattached at the front and decorated with blue rickrack.  A pocket sewn in high up on the right hand side between the seams and lined with pink, blue, white and grey striped cotton. The back decorated on the upper part with thin strips of red felted wool sewn into the seams.
